appendSection.heading: Seat
appendSection.content:
Their seat is [[Bauerholt]], a timber-framed hall in the western woods where the forest thins enough for farming. Of the three woodland branches, the Wilfbauers are the most outward-looking, their farming bringing them into regular contact with the wider world.

## Notable Marriages

House Wilfbauer has provided a bride for a Bramblehall lord as part of the [[Woodland Marriage Tradition]]:
- Woodline Wilfbauer → Bors Wilfrey (~1948)

## Character

The Wilfbauers are practical people — clearers of ground, growers of grain, keepers of livestock. Where the [[House Wilfbole|Wilfboles]] are artisans and the [[House Wilfbark|Wilfbarks]] are hunters, the Wilfbauers feed the forest.

## Current Head

[[Garmund Wilfbauer]] (b. 1955) is master of Bauerholt. His heir is [[Aldmund Wilfbauer]].

**See Also:** [[House Wilfrey of Bramblehall]] · [[Bauerholt]] · [[House Wilfbole]] · [[House Wilfbark]] · [[Woodland Marriage Tradition]]

appendSection.heading: Seat
appendSection.content:
Their seat is [[Bolewood]], built among ancient oaks so vast that some chambers are carved into living trunks. The Wilfboles are carpenters, coopers, and bowyers whose craft is renowned across Bramblehall's lands.

## Notable Marriages

House Wilfbole has provided a bride for a Bramblehall lord as part of the [[Woodland Marriage Tradition]]:
- Beraline Wilfbole → Alec Wilfrey (~1975)

## Character

The most traditional of the three branches. They keep old forest rites that even [[Bramblehall]] has half-forgotten. Their claim that some of their oaks predate the founding of [[House Wilfrey]] is impossible to disprove.

## Current Head

[[Torwin Wilfbole]] (b. 1950) is master of Bolewood. His heir is [[Borwen Wilfbole]].

**See Also:** [[House Wilfrey of Bramblehall]] · [[Bolewood]] · [[House Wilfbauer]] · [[House Wilfbark]] · [[Woodland Marriage Tradition]]

appendSection.heading: Seat
appendSection.content:
Their seat is [[Barkhollow]], a half-underground settlement in a natural depression where three streams converge. Nearly invisible from a distance, Barkhollow reflects the Wilfbarks' role as the hunters, trackers, and wardens of the deep wood.

## Notable Marriages

House Wilfbark has provided brides for Bramblehall's lords as part of the [[Woodland Marriage Tradition]]:
- Mirette Wilfbark → Aldwin Wilfrey (~1825) — the first woodland bride to marry a lord's heir
- Branelisse Wilfbark → Aldric Wilfrey II (~1918)

Borsham Wilfrey (Lord Alec's brother) also married Griseline Wilfbark (~1978).

## Character

The most insular of the three branches — which is saying something among [[Bramblehall]]'s already insular people. The Wilfbarks know every path, clearing, and animal run in the forest. Their knowledge of the deep wood is Bramblehall's greatest strategic asset.

## Current Head

[[Aldhelm Wilfbark]] (b. 1948) is master of Barkhollow. His heir is [[Godhelm Wilfbark]], already reckoned the best tracker of his generation.

**See Also:** [[House Wilfrey of Bramblehall]] · [[Barkhollow]] · [[House Wilfbauer]] · [[House Wilfbole]] · [[Woodland Marriage Tradition]]
